paragraphs: Defense contractors providing intelligence analysis, logistics optimization, and engineering simulations to military ministries must guarantee that classified system prompts, security boundaries, and operational constraints cannot be subverted. Adversarial prompt injection attacks or memory corruption could silently alter rules of engagement or exfiltrate defense design data.

Our sovereign KV-page locking framework seals system prompt attention pages directly inside GPU VRAM using cryptographic hardware memory protection. Once compiled and authenticated with a military multi-signature key, the system prompt KV pages are locked into immutable, read-only memory pages that cannot be overwritten, modified, or evicted by user prompts or malicious inputs.

The locking state machine enforces continuous memory integrity verification. Every subsequent inference pass hashes the system prompt memory pages; any unauthorized alteration triggers an instantaneous hardware security alert, halts active inference sessions, and purges the volatile VRAM within 1.5ms.

Ensuring 100% resistance against prompt injection subversion and memory manipulation, the framework satisfies all requirements of NIST SP 800-171, CMMC Level 3, and DoD Directive 8140, enabling defense contractors to securely serve multi-tenant military workloads with absolute operational integrity.

faqs.question: How does this prevent sophisticated indirect prompt injection attacks?
faqs.answer: The locked system prompt is cryptographically decoupled from the user input context window; user tokens cannot alter the pre-computed attention matrix of the system prompt.

faqs.question: Can authorized defense officers update the system prompt when defense directives change?
faqs.answer: Yes. System prompt updates require dual-custody cryptographic keys issued by an offline defense security manager.

faqs.question: Does memory page locking introduce latency overhead on user queries?
faqs.answer: No. Pre-locking system prompt pages actually eliminates prefill computation time, speeding up user query responses.
